## Summary

There is a high severity vulnerability in Traefik's Kubernetes Ingress NGINX provider where mutual TLS client authentication configured with the `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-secret` annotation is silently disabled for a host when another Ingress declares a path on that same host without the same auth-tls settings. The provider attaches the client-authentication TLS option per Ingress rather than per host, so the conflicting TLS options on the host make Traefik fall back to the default TLS options, which do not request a client certificate, unless `core.strictTLSOptions` is enabled. An unauthenticated remote attacker can then reach the backends that were meant to require a client certificate. Traefik v2 and Traefik v3 versions before v3.7.0 are not affected: support for the `auth-tls-secret` annotation was introduced in v3.7.

## Patches

- https://github.com/traefik/traefik/releases/tag/v3.7.15
